definition: When information from outside the training dataset, particularly from the test or evaluation set, inadvertently influences model training, leading to overly optimistic performance estimates.
details: Data leakage is a common and often subtle pitfall in ML pipelines, and can occur through improper data splitting, duplicate records across splits, or benchmark contamination in large web-scraped training corpora.
story: Think of a historian sorting through boxes of letters, building a picture of an era one sentence at a time. In plain words: When information from outside the training dataset, particularly from the test or evaluation set, inadvertently influences model training, leading to overly optimistic performance estimates. Here is how it actually plays out: Data leakage is a common and often subtle pitfall in ML pipelines, and can occur through improper data splitting, duplicate records across splits, or benchmark contamination in large web-scraped training corpora. The words a model reads become the world it believes in. That care with the raw material is Data Leakage.
